corrected_statement: By the §21.6 definition (plan lines 4521–4524), for a cell with no applicable identity 'reproduced' reduces to extraction fidelity; this deduction is valid. On the ten known workbooks, 41–46% of numeric cells sit in no instance of the plan's named identities (T1 attributable = ownership × 100%; Σ components, read as T2 flow sums, T6 physical sums and T8 capex; T5 cumulative additivity; T3 sold-weighted roll-up). The figures are 7,784 of P03's 18,860 cells (41.3%), 6,705 of 15,605 site cells (43.0%) and 748 of 1,633 first-publication quarterly M0 per-site fields (45.8%). Whether the 95% bar is then 'met mainly by a correct parser' depends on a reading the plan leaves open. If an identity failure disqualifies only the derived cell, failures remove 0.3–2.0% of cells and a correct extractor clears 95% (ceiling 98.0–99.7%), so the headline mainly measures extraction. If it disqualifies every participating cell, no extractor reaches 95% (ceiling 82.7–94.3%). Under either reading the headline alone hides the identity-checked share, so it should be reported separately. 'Equals the published cell' also needs a reference read independent of the importer, such as BD-271's 3,996 hand-checked cells; otherwise the importer is compared with itself.

corrected_statement: Arithmetic verified. The plan implies about 1,030–1,070 non-blank Rust LOC per calendar day: 390k in phase A over M0–M2 = months 0–12 (§28.3 line 6340, §37.3 line 7421) gives 1,068/day, and 1,128k over 36 months gives 1,029/day. That is close to the slowest sibling (1,106). At sibling rates the 1,298k ceiling would be reached in about 12.0 months at the median, 3.8–4.7 months at Q3 depending on the quantile method, and 1.1 months at the maximum. Phase-A tests at 6.3–9.5 per kLOC come to 2,457–3,705. Forecast, unscored: code volume is unlikely to be what binds M0–M2 dates. Data gates, reviewers and site access are more likely to bind, and if code does run near sibling rates, the §28.4 80/100/115% triggers would fire within months. Scoreable form: over the first 60 days, FrankenMining's non-blank LOC/day and its count of days blocked by a pending human or external gate. The forecast is reversed if LOC/day < 1,100 while no gate is pending.

The reference-class comparison is the main weakness: most siblings port reference libraries with existing oracles and conformance suites, while FrankenMining is a new domain with external data and human gates. That difference strengthens the 'something other than code binds' branch but makes LOC rates a weak predictor of schedule.

decision_impact: Frame §28/RISK-25 around gates and review capacity rather than LOC throughput; keep the §28.4 triggers.
